Credits are awarded by CHS, which accepts credits from other accredited secondary schools, including summer school. | In order for a student to participate in the graduation ceremony, they must have completed the twenty-four and a half (24.5) graduation requirements. | Each department has delineated 2-8 discipline-specific proficiencies that a student is required to meet for graduation (CHS Essential Expectations and CHS Discipline Proficiencies); credit is awarded upon demonstration of proficiency. | All students will develop a Personal Learning Plan (PLP) that will evolve grades 9-12. | English: students must be enrolled in an English course for all four of their Blue House semesters and earn at least 2 English credits in the Blue House (4 over 4 years). All juniors must enroll in T.H.E.E. or AP English Language; seniors must enroll in Seminar (0.5 English + 0.5 social studies). | Social Studies: students must be enrolled in a social studies course for three of four Blue House semesters and earn at least 1.5 social studies credits in the Blue House (3.5 over 4 years). Middle school Algebra I earns one elective credit upon entering the high school, but all students must complete 3.5 math credits at the high school. | Science: three and a half credits including Biology, Earth Systems Science or AP Environmental Science, and one full year of physical science (Chemistry or Physics). | Fine Arts: students must complete one fine arts credit for graduation, in either visual art or music. | Health: one semester of health (normally Human Ecology in the Green House; Life 101 in the Blue House). | Physical Education: three semesters (Blue House and/or Green House). | Options credits: up to two (2.0) options credits may be earned during high school and applied toward elective credit only; options credit and independent study may not be used to fulfill content-specific/core graduation requirements. | All students must carry 6.0 credits (6 of 8 mods of academic classes) each semester. | One high school elective credit may be granted for Developing or better in level one World Language at CMS. | Colchester High School will provide students the opportunity to experience learning through flexible pathways, including career and technical education, virtual learning, work-based learning, service learning, dual enrollment, and early college.
